newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Red Cross body asked to intervene after crash.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross body asked to intervene after crash.

text.p: Georgia said on Tuesday it had asked for the diplomatic immunity of a Red Cross official working in the former Soviet republic to be lifted so it can investigate a weekend car accident in which two men died.

Tbilisi Chief Prosecutor Nugzar Gabrichidze told Reuters two men were killed when a four-wheel drive Red Cross vehicle driven by 65-year-old Alexander Marinov, a Bulgarian national, was involved in a collision early on Sunday.
Marinov is head of the Georgian branch of the Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC). He was not immediately available for comment.

Foreign Minister Irakly Menagarishvili told reporters in Tbilisi that Georgia had sent a note to the Geneva headquarters of the Federation asking for Marinov's immunity to be lifted to "guarantee an objective investigation."
He said the IFRC has so far not lifted Marinov's immunity, but that on Tuesday it had agreed to allow him to be questioned by investigators.

In Geneva, IFRC spokesman Jon Valfells said the Federation was in close contact and cooperating fully with the Georgian authorities over the affair. "We want it investigated, just as they do," he added.

But he said no decision had yet been taken on the immunity request. Many heads of IFRC delegations -- the term the Federation uses for major offices around the world -- have diplomatic status by agreement with the national government.
Valfells said IFRC Secretary-General George Weber had sent letters of condolences over the accident to Georgia's President Eduard Shevardnadze and to the relatives of the two who died.
The Federation, which specialises in disaster relief, is an umbrella body uniting national Red Cross and Red Crescent societies around the globe.
It is active in Georgia, where thousands were killed and many more made refugees by civil conflicts after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
